title: Transfer Learning Through Conditional Quantile Matching
claim: Calibrating a weighted combination of source conditional distributions makes it match the target's conditional distribution at a fixed covariate.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, approximation equation between matched curves, dashed arrows entering from above
description: The crop shows two small hand-drawn style plots with axes, each containing a bell-shaped density curve. On the left, a solid purple curve is labeled 'Conditional quantile matching' below it. On the right, a dark-red dash-dotted curve is labeled 'Target domain' in larger type. Between them, a purple-and-red equation reads sum over k=1..K of beta_k Y^(k) | X=x ≈ Y^(0) | X=x, with a large black approximation sign in the middle. abstract: We introduce a transfer learning framework for regression that leverages heterogeneous source domains to improve predictive performance in a data-scarce target domain. Our approach fits a conditional generative model to each source domain and calibrates a shared linear combination of the generated responses via conditional quantile matching at the observed target covariates. The calibration aligns the conditional response distributions while accommodating simultaneous shifts in both the covariate and conditional response distributions. The calibrated responses then serve as pseudo-labels to augment the target data for a broad class of downstream learning tasks. Theoretically, we derive an excess risk bound for an empirical risk minimizer (ERM) trained on the augmented data, separating the benefit of an enlarged training sample from errors due to density ratio estimation, source generator estimation, conditional calibration, and irreducible transfer bias. Empirically, simulations and real-data applications show that the proposed method can improve target-domain prediction when the transfer bias is small.
